editorial:
Set in Yokohama in 1963, this gentle animated story follows Umi, a hardworking high school girl who runs her family’s boarding house and raises signal flags each morning. When she meets Shun, a bold student fighting to save an old clubhouse, their friendship grows into something deeper. The film wraps you in a warm, nostalgic mood, showing a Japan rebuilding after war while young people try to honor the past without getting stuck in it. You feel the salt air, busy streets, and quiet family moments in every scene.

The hand-drawn animation is gorgeous, with soft colors and careful details that make everyday life feel special. The characters feel real, and the romance stays sweet without rushing. On the downside, the pace is slow, and there is not much action, so viewers wanting big thrills may lose interest. Still, if you enjoy thoughtful coming-of-age stories, this is a lovely pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or watch it on 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Umi and Shun learn the painful truth about their fathers and their possible family connection, which makes them pull apart. Later, after more digging, they discover they are not related, so the secret no longer blocks their future. The film ends with them together again, looking toward a brighter tomorrow, while the old clubhouse is saved and the school community celebrates. It closes on hope, not sadness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt animated stories and quiet romance.
